usage_example.sesotho: Ka letsatsi la bobeli Molimo a phetha mosebetsi oa hae.
usage_example.english: By the second day God finished His work.

senses.definition_en: to set apart as holy, to consecrate

usage_example.sesotho: Molimo a halaletsa letsatsi la bosupa.
usage_example.english: God sanctified the seventh day.

senses.definition_en: a woody plant smaller than a tree, with several stems; a bush

usage_example.sesotho: Ha ho a ba le sehlahla sa naha hofatše.
usage_example.english: No shrub of the field was yet in the earth.

senses.definition_en: the upper layer of earth in which plants grow; the ground

usage_example.sesotho: Jehova Molimo a etsa motho ka lerōle la mobu.
usage_example.english: The LORD God formed man from the dust of the soil.

morphology.derivation: Common noun for a cultivated plot

senses.definition_en: a piece of ground used for growing flowers, fruit, or vegetables

usage_example.sesotho: Jehova Molimo a lema serapa Edene, ka ng'a bochabela.
usage_example.english: The LORD God planted a garden eastward in Eden.

morphology.derivation: From 'chaba' (to rise, of the sun) + 'ela' (applied suffix)

senses.definition_en: the direction where the sun rises

usage_example.sesotho: Jehova Molimo a lema serapa Edene, ka ng'a bochabela.
usage_example.english: The LORD God planted a garden eastward in Eden.

senses.definition_en: a woody perennial plant, typically large, with a single trunk and branches

usage_example.sesotho: Joale Jehova Molimo a mela le sefate sohle se khabisehang lefatšeng.
usage_example.english: The LORD God made to grow every tree that is pleasant to the sight.

senses.definition_en: facts, information, and skills acquired through experience or education; awareness or familiarity

usage_example.sesotho: ...le sefate sa tsebo ea molemo le bokhopo.
usage_example.english: ...and the tree of the knowledge of good and evil.

senses.definition_en: a large natural stream of water flowing in a channel

usage_example.sesotho: Joale ho ne ho e-na le nōka e tsoang Edene ho nosetsa serapa seo.
usage_example.english: Now a river went out of Eden to water the garden.

senses.definition_en: a yellow precious metal, chemical element Au

usage_example.sesotho: ...naha eohle ea Havila, moo ho nang le khauta.
usage_example.english: ...the whole land of Havilah, where there is gold.

senses.definition_en: a piece of rock or hard mineral substance; a precious stone or gem

usage_example.sesotho: ...le lejoe la oli le lijoe tsa topaze.
usage_example.english: ...and the onyx stone and the stone of beryl.

senses.definition_en: to prepare and use land for crops or gardening

usage_example.sesotho: Jehova Molimo a nka motho a mo beha serapeng sa Edene ho se lema.
usage_example.english: Then the LORD God took the man and put him in the garden of Eden to tend it.

senses.definition_en: to look after, keep, or tend to something

usage_example.sesotho: Jehova Molimo a nka motho a mo beha serapeng sa Edene ho se lema le ho se hlokomela.
usage_example.english: The LORD God took the man and put him in the garden of Eden to tend and keep it.

senses.definition_en: to give an authoritative order or instruction

usage_example.sesotho: Jehova Molimo a boela a laela motho sena.
usage_example.english: And the LORD God commanded the man, saying...

morphology.derivation: Deverbative from 'thusa' (to help) with personal prefix 'mo-'

senses.definition_en: a person who helps or supports someone else

usage_example.sesotho: Ke tla mo etsetsa mothusi, e be motlatsi oa hae.
usage_example.english: I will make him a helper comparable to him.

senses.definition_en: a complement or counterpart; one who fills what is lacking in another

usage_example.sesotho: Ke tla mo etsetsa mothusi, e be motlatsi oa hae.
usage_example.english: I will make him a helper, a complement for him.

senses.definition_en: to give a name to someone or something

usage_example.sesotho: O qala ho li tlisa ho motho ho bona hore na se seng le se seng sa tsona o tla se reha eng.
usage_example.english: And brought them to Adam to see what he would call them.

morphology.derivation: Deverbative abstract noun from 'robala' (to sleep), prefix bo-

senses.definition_en: a deep, heavy state of sleeping; the natural periodic suspension of consciousness

usage_example.sesotho: Jehova Molimo a etsa monna a robale boroko bo boholo.
usage_example.english: The LORD God caused a deep sleep to fall on the man.

senses.definition_en: one of the curved bones that protect the thorax

usage_example.sesotho: A nka e 'ngoe ea likhopo tsa hae 'me sebakeng sa eona a koala ka nama.
usage_example.english: And He took one of his ribs, and closed up the flesh in its place.

senses.definition_en: the soft substance of the body of a person or animal, consisting of muscle and fat; physical nature

usage_example.sesotho: A nka e 'ngoe ea likhopo tsa hae 'me sebakeng sa eona a koala ka nama.
usage_example.english: And He took one of his ribs, and closed up the flesh in its place.

senses.definition_en: an adult female human being; a female partner in a marriage

usage_example.sesotho: Eaba Jehova Molimo o etsa mosali ka khopo eo a e nkileng ho monna.
usage_example.english: Then the rib which the LORD God had taken from man He made into a woman.

senses.definition_en: any of the pieces of hard tissue making up the skeleton

usage_example.sesotho: Qetellong enoa ke lesapo la masapo a ka.
usage_example.english: This is now bone of my bones.

senses.definition_en: to go away from; to depart and forsake

usage_example.sesotho: Ka hona monna o tla siea ntata hae le 'mae 'me o tla khumamelana le mosali oa hae.
usage_example.english: Therefore a man shall leave his father and his mother and be joined to his wife.
